record.original_question: Suppose Ik(T) = T P_{k^2}(log T) + O(T^(1/2 + epsilon)) conjecturally, where P_{k^2} is a polynomial of degree k^2, and define the error term by Ek(T) = Ik(T) - T P_{k^2}(log T). Determine the optimal exponents theta_k for which Ek(T) = O(T^(theta_k + epsilon)) should hold for each integer k, especially for k >= 3, and decide whether the Multiple Dirichlet Series method can justify the correct conjectural values.

evidence.quote: It would be desirable to come up with a conjecture for optimal constants θk such that Ek (T ) = O(T^(θk + epsilon)) holds for k in N. N. Ng believes that θ1 = 1/4 and θ2 = 1/2 are the correct answers for k = 1, 2. What about k >= 3? Both Ivic and Motohashi suggested θ3 = 3/4. Can the Multiple Dirichlet Series method be used to derive an appropriate conjecture?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $k\ge 1$ and $T\ge 2$, let
$$I_k(T)=\int_0^T\bigl|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)\bigr|^{2k}\,dt,$$
where $\zeta$ denotes the Riemann zeta function. It is conjectured that there exists a polynomial $P_{k^2}$ of degree $k^2$ (with leading coefficient predicted by the Conrey–Ghosh / Keating–Snaith / Conrey–Farmer–Keating–Rubinstein–Snaith heuristics) such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$I_k(T)=T\,P_{k^2}(\log T)+O\!\bigl(T^{1/2+\varepsilon}\bigr).$$
Define the error term
$$E_k(T)=I_k(T)-T\,P_{k^2}(\log T).$$

(a) Determine the optimal (i.e., infimal) exponent $\theta_k\in[0,1]$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$E_k(T)=O\!\bigl(T^{\theta_k+\varepsilon}\bigr).$$
In particular, decide whether $\theta_1=1/4$ and $\theta_2=1/2$, and determine $\theta_k$ for all $k\ge 3$ (it has been suggested that $\theta_3=3/4$).

(b) Decide whether the Multiple Dirichlet Series method can be used to derive the correct conjectural values of $\theta_k$.
artifact.category_tag: moments of the Riemann zeta function
artifact.status_search_result: The exact size of the error term $E_k(T)$ in the moment asymptotics for $|\zeta(1/2+it)|^{2k}$ remains open for all $k\ge 1$. Even for $k=2$, only partial bounds on $E_2(T)$ are known and being improved (e.g., recent 2025 work on the fourth-moment error term). No asymptotic for $I_k(T)$ has been proved for any $k\ge 3$, so optimal exponents $\theta_k$ for $k\ge 3$ remain conjectural. There is no published derivation of these values via Multiple Dirichlet Series.

status_evidence.title: On the error term of the fourth moment of the Riemann zeta-function
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bounds on the error term E_2(T) in the fourth moment, improving log-power factors but not reaching the conjectured exponent 1/2.
status_evidence.claim: The optimal size of E_2(T) is still unknown; only upper bounds are improved.

status_evidence.title: High moments of the Riemann zeta-function (Conrey–Gonek)
status_evidence.snippet: No asymptotic formula has been proved for any moment higher than the fourth.
status_evidence.claim: For k>=3 the leading-term asymptotic is itself only conjectural, so optimal theta_k is open.

status_evidence.title: Moments of zeta and correlations of divisor sums (AIM workshop)
status_evidence.snippet: Workshop on conjectural moment asymptotics and error terms; problems on optimal exponents listed as open.
status_evidence.claim: Determining sharp exponents for E_k(T) is an open problem in the field.
